menswear.tip: Shoulder seams should sit at the edge of your shoulders; most fit problems elsewhere can be tailored.
A slight break (one soft fold at the shoe) suits most trousers; slim trousers look best with no break.
Untucked shirts should end around mid-fly; if it covers your seat, it's meant to be tucked.
A blazer should cover your seat; casual jackets look best ending at the belt.
Go from thin to thick: tee, then shirt or overshirt, then jacket.
Linen and cotton for hot, humid days; wool blends for air-conditioned offices and cooler months.

womenswear.tip: Choose one focus area per outfit — a fitted top with relaxed bottoms, or the reverse.
Hem trousers for the shoes you'll wear most; midi skirts look best ending just below the widest part of the calf.
A front tuck, a belt or a wrap is optional — use it when you want to mark the waist.
Long open layers add length; cropped layers mark the waist.
Cotton, linen and rayon breathe in heat; structured fabrics hold shape for work.
If you can't sit, reach or walk easily, the fit is wrong — not you.

unisex.tip: Pair one roomy piece with one neater piece so the outfit keeps shape.
A slight crop at the ankle suits sneakers and loafers; full length suits boots.
Build around a base tee or shirt, then add an overshirt, knit or jacket.
Stick to two or three palette shades per outfit for easy mixing.
Choose breathable cotton and linen for heat; heavier twill and wool for cooler days.
Relaxed shouldn't mean sloppy — check the shoulders still sit near your shoulder line.

Hourglass: Most cuts work — tailored and regular fits follow your balanced frame.
A belt at the natural waist keeps outfits neat.
Rectangle: Layering and texture add depth to an even build.
Waist points — a belt, a tucked shirt or a waist-length jacket — add shape.
Crew necks and patterned shirts add interest up top.
Pear: Structure and detail on top — collars, chest pockets, structured shoulders — balance the hips.
Darker, straight or relaxed trousers keep the lower half simple.
Avoid very skinny trousers that emphasise the hip-to-ankle contrast.
Apple: Open layers and straight hems create vertical lines.
Mid-rise trousers with a comfortable waistband sit better than low-rise.
Choose fabrics that drape rather than cling, and avoid tight knits.
Inverted Triangle: V-necks and open collars narrow the shoulder line.
Straight, relaxed or pleated trousers balance the upper body.
Soft-shouldered jackets don't add extra width.

Hourglass: Wrap, sweetheart and V necklines echo your balanced proportions.
Fabrics with gentle drape and stretch keep the waist defined.
Belt longer layers at the natural waist rather than the hips.
Rectangle: Scoop, sweetheart and square necklines add softness.
Cropped jackets over high-waisted pieces create a waist point.
Textured or pleated fabrics add movement.
Pear: Boat, off-shoulder and square necklines bring attention upward.
Darker or simpler bottoms with brighter tops create balance.
Straight-leg, bootcut and flared shapes fall smoothly from the hip.
Apple: V and scoop necklines create a vertical line.
Open long layers such as cardigans or dusters add length.
Soft, structured fabrics that drape rather than cling feel comfortable.
Inverted Triangle: Scoop, V and halter necklines soften the shoulder line.
A-line skirts, wide-leg trousers and prints add interest below the waist.
Keep shoulder details minimal and let lower-half pieces carry volume.

Hourglass: Most cuts work; relaxed pieces look best with one defined point, like a tucked hem.
Rectangle: Boxy jackets ending at the hip add shape.
Pear: Keep volume and detail on top; choose straight bottoms.
Darker trousers with lighter tops create balance.
Apple: Open layers and straight hems create vertical lines.
Inverted Triangle: Relaxed or wide trousers balance the upper body.
Soft shoulders and open collars narrow the line.

face_items.title: Textured crop
face_items.desc: Short sides with choppy texture on top.
face_items.tip: Ask for scissor-cut texture on top with a low or mid taper; style with a matte clay.

shapes.Oval: Short, textured cuts suit balanced proportions.
shapes.Round: Texture on top adds height; keep the sides short.
shapes.Diamond: A short fringe adds width at the forehead.

face_items.title: Crew cut
face_items.desc: A classic short cut, slightly longer at the front.
face_items.tip: A trim every 3–4 weeks keeps it sharp.

shapes.Oval: A clean, classic option for balanced features.

face_items.title: Side part
face_items.desc: A tidy parting with a little length on top.
face_items.tip: A natural part grows out more gracefully than a shaved 'hard' part.

shapes.Round: An off-centre part adds asymmetry and length.
shapes.Square: A soft side part balances strong angles.
shapes.Heart: A low side part with some fringe narrows a wider forehead.

face_items.title: Quiff
face_items.desc: Lift and movement at the front.
face_items.tip: Blow-dry upwards and finish with a light paste.

shapes.Round: Lift at the front elongates the face.
shapes.Oval: Height works well with balanced proportions.
shapes.Square: Volume on top balances a strong jaw.

face_items.title: Pompadour
face_items.desc: Swept-back volume with shorter sides.
face_items.tip: Needs daily styling with a pomade and blow-dryer.

shapes.Round: Height at the crown makes the face look longer.

face_items.title: Fade variations
face_items.desc: Low, mid or skin fades under a longer top.
face_items.tip: Low fades grow out softer; skin fades need a trim every 2–3 weeks.

shapes.Round: A mid or high fade slims the sides.
shapes.Square: A fade keeps a strong jaw the focus.
shapes.Diamond: A low fade keeps some width at the temples.

face_items.title: Buzz cut
face_items.desc: Even, very short length all over.
face_items.tip: A 2–4 guard is common; go longer for a softer look.

face_items.title: Medium-length textured
face_items.desc: Loose, ear-length layers with movement.
face_items.tip: A sea-salt spray on damp hair adds texture.

shapes.Square: Movement at the sides softens angles.
shapes.Heart: Length around the ears adds width lower down.

face_items.title: Curly top with taper
face_items.desc: Defined curls on top with tapered sides.
face_items.tip: Apply curl cream to damp hair and avoid brushing curls when dry.

shapes.Round: Keeping curls taller than wide adds length.
shapes.Heart: Keep some volume at the sides.
shapes.Diamond: Curls at the fringe widen the forehead.

face_items.title: Short twists or natural coils
face_items.desc: Defined coils or twists with a neat edge.
face_items.tip: Moisturise regularly and sleep on a satin pillowcase to reduce frizz.

face_items.title: Longer hairstyles
face_items.desc: Shoulder-length hair with long layers.
face_items.tip: Long layers stop it sitting bulky; tie it into a low bun for formal events.

shapes.Heart: Length near the jaw balances the forehead.
shapes.Round: Keep length past the chin with face-framing layers.

face_items.title: Top knot or low bun
face_items.desc: Long hair tied back neatly.
face_items.tip: Use a soft elastic to avoid breakage.

face_items.title: Pixie cut
face_items.desc: Cropped and textured, with soft pieces at the front.
face_items.tip: Book a trim every 4–6 weeks to keep the shape.

shapes.Oval: Short cuts show off balanced features.
shapes.Heart: A side-swept pixie with a soft fringe narrows the forehead.
shapes.Diamond: Fullness at the forehead balances cheekbones.

face_items.title: Chin-length bob
face_items.desc: A classic bob with soft ends.
face_items.tip: Soft, textured ends feel easier than a blunt line at the jaw.

shapes.Oval: A versatile length for balanced features.
shapes.Heart: Volume at the chin balances a narrower chin.
shapes.Diamond: Fullness at the jaw balances cheekbones.
shapes.Square: A slightly longer, textured bob softens the jaw.

face_items.title: Layered lob
face_items.desc: A long bob with soft layers.
face_items.tip: Ask for layers starting just below the chin.

shapes.Round: Falling below the chin elongates the face.
shapes.Heart: Fullness near the jaw balances the forehead.

face_items.title: Long layers
face_items.desc: Movement while keeping length.
face_items.tip: Face-framing layers can start at the cheekbones or chin.

shapes.Round: Layers starting below the chin lengthen.

face_items.title: Curtain bangs
face_items.desc: A soft, centre-parted fringe.
face_items.tip: Blow-dry with a round brush away from the face.

shapes.Square: Softens a strong forehead and jaw.
shapes.Heart: Parted bangs narrow a wider forehead.

face_items.title: Wispy fringe
face_items.desc: A light, see-through fringe.
face_items.tip: Trim the fringe every 3–4 weeks.

shapes.Heart: Softens a wider forehead.
shapes.Diamond: Widens the look of a narrow forehead.
shapes.Oval: A soft frame for the eyes.

face_items.title: Side-swept curtain fringe
face_items.desc: A longer fringe swept to one side.
face_items.tip: Grows out easily into face-framing layers.

face_items.title: Soft waves
face_items.desc: Loose waves for movement.
face_items.tip: Heat-free: braid damp hair overnight. With heat: use protection spray.

shapes.Diamond: Volume at the jaw balances cheekbones.

face_items.title: Curly shag
face_items.desc: Layered curls with volume at the crown.
face_items.tip: Ask for a dry cut or a stylist experienced with curls.

shapes.Heart: Volume lower down balances the forehead.

face_items.title: Crown-lift ponytail
face_items.desc: A ponytail with height at the crown.
face_items.tip: Tease lightly at the crown before tying.

face_items.title: Low ponytail
face_items.desc: A sleek or soft low ponytail.
face_items.tip: Wrap a strand around the elastic for a polished finish.

shapes.Heart: A low line balances the forehead.

face_items.title: Ponytail with face-framing pieces
face_items.desc: A ponytail with curtain pieces left out at the front.
face_items.tip: Leave out two front sections before tying.

shapes.Heart: Front pieces soften the forehead.

face_items.title: Low bun or updo
face_items.desc: A polished updo for formal and festive days.
face_items.tip: Leave a few face-framing pieces loose.

face_items.title: Buzz cut
face_items.desc: Even, very short length.
face_items.tip: A slightly longer guard on top keeps it soft.

face_items.title: Crop with soft fringe
face_items.desc: Short sides and a forward-brushed fringe.
face_items.tip: Point-cut the fringe so it isn't too heavy.

shapes.Heart: Softens the forehead.

face_items.title: Undercut with length on top
face_items.desc: Shorter sides with a longer top you can sweep or part.
face_items.tip: Tidy the sides every 3–4 weeks.

shapes.Square: Length on top balances the jaw.

face_items.title: Modern shag
face_items.desc: Choppy layers with movement.
face_items.tip: Air-dry with a light texture spray.

shapes.Heart: Volume at the jaw balances the forehead.

face_items.title: Chin-length cut
face_items.desc: A blunt or textured cut around the chin.
face_items.tip: Tuck one side behind the ear for asymmetry.

shapes.Heart: Volume at the chin balances the forehead.
shapes.Diamond: Fullness at the jaw balances cheekbones.

face_items.title: Shoulder-length layers
face_items.desc: Loose layers that sit at the shoulders.
face_items.tip: Wear down, half-up or tied back.

face_items.title: Shaped natural curls
face_items.desc: Curls cut to their natural shape.
face_items.tip: Find a stylist who cuts curls dry, curl by curl.

face_items.title: Long and loose
face_items.desc: Long hair with minimal layers.
face_items.tip: A trim every 8–12 weeks keeps ends healthy.

face_items.title: Round frames
face_items.desc: Soft circles that contrast with angles.
face_items.tip: Make sure the frame is about as wide as your face at the temples.

shapes.Heart: Light round frames soften the forehead.

face_items.title: Rectangular frames
face_items.desc: Clean lines for structure.
face_items.tip: A slightly wider-than-tall lens suits most faces.

shapes.Heart: A slim rectangle keeps the upper face light.

face_items.title: Aviator-inspired frames
face_items.desc: A teardrop shape, wider at the bottom.
face_items.tip: Thin metal aviators feel lighter for everyday wear.

shapes.Heart: A wider lower edge balances a broader forehead.
shapes.Square: The curved bottom softens the jaw.

face_items.title: Browline frames
face_items.desc: A bold upper rim with a thin lower rim.
face_items.tip: The top rim should follow your eyebrows.

shapes.Diamond: A strong brow line widens the forehead.
shapes.Round: The defined upper line adds structure.

face_items.title: Square acetate frames
face_items.desc: Thick, slightly oversized square frames.
face_items.tip: Check that your eyes sit near the centre of each lens.

shapes.Diamond: A wider top line balances cheekbones.

face_items.title: Cat-eye frames
face_items.desc: An upswept outer edge for a lifted look.
face_items.tip: Subtle upsweeps are easiest for everyday wear.

face_items.title: Lightweight semi-rimless frames
face_items.desc: Minimal frames that feel light all day.
face_items.tip: A good everyday choice if you wear glasses for long hours.

shapes.Heart: Keeps the upper face light.

face_items.title: Watches
face_items.desc: A simple dial on leather or metal.
face_items.tip: Match the metal to your undertone and the strap to your belt.

shapes.Round: A rectangular dial adds an angular accent.
shapes.Square: A round dial softens the overall look.

face_items.title: Fine chains
face_items.desc: A thin chain worn under an open collar.
face_items.tip: Keep it close to the collarbone.

shapes.Round: A slightly longer chain creates a vertical line.

face_items.title: Caps & hats
face_items.desc: Baseball caps, beanies or bucket hats.
face_items.tip: Choose crown height to suit your face length.

shapes.Heart: A wider brim balances the forehead.

face_items.title: Bracelets
face_items.desc: Leather, bead or metal bracelets.
face_items.tip: Wear on the wrist opposite your watch.

face_items.title: Small studs or huggie hoops
face_items.desc: Minimal earrings for pierced ears.
face_items.tip: One metal tone keeps it cohesive.

face_items.title: Statement earrings
face_items.desc: Hoops and chandeliers that highlight the cheekbones.
face_items.tip: Keep the necklace simple when the earrings are bold.

face_items.title: Hoop earrings
face_items.desc: Rounded hoops that soften angles.
face_items.tip: Medium hoops are the most versatile.

face_items.title: Long drop earrings
face_items.desc: Linear earrings that add length.
face_items.tip: Lightweight drops are comfortable all day.

face_items.title: Chokers
face_items.desc: A short necklace that adds width at the neck.
face_items.tip: Pair with an open neckline.

shapes.Heart: Adds width near a narrower chin.

face_items.title: Ear cuffs
face_items.desc: A modern accent along the ear.
face_items.tip: No piercing needed for most cuffs.

shapes.Heart: Keeps focus near the cheekbones.

face_items.title: Cluster earrings
face_items.desc: Small, layered stones close to the ear.
face_items.tip: Great for festive outfits without heavy drops.

shapes.Diamond: Adds width at the ear line.

face_items.title: V-shaped necklaces
face_items.desc: Pendants that form a V.
face_items.tip: Match the V to your neckline.

face_items.title: Long pendants
face_items.desc: A single pendant on a longer chain.
face_items.tip: Sits best over plain fabrics.

face_items.title: Round pendant necklaces
face_items.desc: Soft circular pendants.
face_items.tip: Choose a chain that sits just below the collarbone.

face_items.title: Layered necklaces
face_items.desc: Two or three fine chains at different lengths.
face_items.tip: Keep 4–5 cm between layers so they don't tangle.

face_items.title: Hair clips
face_items.desc: Claw clips and barrettes for quick styling.
face_items.tip: A claw clip makes a quick, soft twist-up.

menswear.tip: Short cuts and fades look best trimmed every 2–4 weeks; longer styles every 6–8 weeks.
Matte clay or paste for texture, cream for a natural finish, curl cream for curls — use a pea-sized amount.
If you want tidier brows, remove only stray hairs between them and keep the natural shape.
Wear one watch and keep other accessories to one or two pieces in the same metal tone.
Face soft window light, hold the camera at eye level and wear a solid palette shade near your face.

womenswear.tip: Short cuts and fringes need a trim every 4–6 weeks; longer hair every 8–12 weeks.
Use a heat-protection spray before hot tools, and let hair air-dry when you can.
Brow shaping is optional — if you shape them, follow your natural arch.
Let one area lead: bold earrings or a statement necklace, not both.
Face soft window light, hold the camera at eye level and wear a solid palette shade near your face.

unisex.tip: Short cuts look best trimmed every 3–5 weeks; longer styles every 8–12 weeks.
A light texture spray or cream suits most cuts; curl cream for curls.
Tidy only if you want to; keeping your natural shape always works.
Pick one metal tone and repeat it across glasses, jewellery and watch.
Face soft window light, hold the camera at eye level and wear a solid palette shade near your face.

Warm.summary: Warm undertones are usually flattered by golden metals and warm leathers.

Cool.summary: Cool undertones are usually flattered by silver-toned metals and cool, dark leathers.

Neutral.summary: Neutral undertones can wear both warm and cool metals, so mixing is easy.

avoid_guidance.menswear: If you love them, wear these as trousers, shoes or a bag rather than shirts, ties or collars near your face.
avoid_guidance.womenswear: If you love them, wear these as skirts, trousers, shoes or bags rather than tops, scarves or earrings near your face.
avoid_guidance.unisex: If you love them, wear these away from your face — trousers, shoes or a bag — rather than tops or collars.
